prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's critical-pair locality term (coefficient 2.0, c056 +0.134) is the only mechanism that pays off; scaling it modestly upward (x2 to 4.0 was tested as c056 and helped C1 but stayed flat elsewhere) — instead I combine it with a mild hinge-style dead-band on the area balance so the raw partition stays near 50% without a flat quadratic, reducing repair flips (rho=+0.48 with score) while keeping the locality strength unchanged.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=+0.057 robust(mean-std)=-0.055 min_case=-0.063 seed_std=0.078 tns_mean=+0.043 all_valid=True
  C1: score=+0.117 dWNS=+12.8% dTNS=+11.8% per-seed=[+0.09 +0.05 +0.21]
  C2: score=-0.063 dWNS=-14.9% dTNS=-0.6% per-seed=[-0.21 +0.03 -0.01]
  C3: score=+0.003 dWNS=-0.9% dTNS=+2.6% per-seed=[-0.08 +0.04 +0.05]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->136, wcut 421->399, crit_cross 0.011->0.005, repair_flips 103->119, changed-vs-baseline 15.3%
  C2: cut 318->309, wcut 1007->980, crit_cross 0.000->0.000, repair_flips 238->251, changed-vs-baseline 6.1%
  C3: cut 582->581, wcut 1955->1947, crit_cross 0.069->0.065, repair_flips 353->348, changed-vs-baseline 4.5%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response: (1) Partially: C1 improved (+0.117) with crit_cross halved (0.011→0.005) and wcut down, but C2 regressed (-0.063, dWNS -14.9%) and C3 flat; repair_flips rose on C1/C2, contradicting the intended flip reduction. (2) Locality term helped C1 via fewer critical-pair crossings; C2's cut reduction didn't translate to timing, suggesting the dead-band shifted balance without net benefit. (3) Seed spread is high (std 0.078, C2 per-seed -0.21 to +0.03) — not acceptable. (4) Ablate the dead-band alone vs. locality-alone on C2 to isolate the regression before retuning.
